title: One-sided anodyne factorization of an indexing equivalence
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories and functor equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], right anodyne maps from [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], and trivial Kan fibrations (lifting every boundary inclusion, including the empty boundary in dimension zero) from [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. If $e:L\to M$ is a functor equivalence between small quasicategories in a fixed universe, there exist a small quasicategory $N$ in that universe and simplicial maps
$$L\xrightarrow{i}N\xrightarrow{r}M$$
such that $ri=e$ exactly, $i$ is a degreewise injective right anodyne map, and $r$ is a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.1.15, right-cofinal/right-anodyne version, applied using Corollary 7.2.1.13 (02NC), which makes categorical equivalences right cofinal. The intermediate object is a quasicategory because its trivial Kan fibration to M lifts inner horns. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; online source read, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] in the category of small simplicial sets to the countable family $I=\{\Lambda_j^d\hookrightarrow\Delta^d\mid d\geq1,\ 0<j\leq d\}$, with $\kappa=\aleph_0$. Here are its smallness checks. Hom sets are small sets of compatible degreewise functions. Small colimits exist: in each degree take the disjoint union of the diagram's sets modulo the relations imposed by its arrows; every simplicial operator descends to this quotient, and the resulting compatible maps satisfy the colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Each horn is the union of finitely many representable faces. A map from it to a sequential colimit of degreewise injections is specified by the images of those finitely many faces, subject to finitely many overlap equations: choose a common stage for their images and then a later common stage for the equations. The same finite argument detects equality of two such maps. Successor pushouts of coproducts of the horn inclusions are degreewise injective: a set pushout along an injection adds the complement without identifying distinct old elements. This verifies the required preservation of these chain colimits. The cited factorization therefore supplies small maps $L\xrightarrow{i}N\xrightarrow{r}M$ with $ri=e$, $i$ an $I$-cell map and $r$ lifting every member of $I$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.7 (014Z), whose displayed construction attaches left horns; apply its simplicial-opposite right-handed dual through the existing general small-object leaf after the explicit finite-domain and degreewise-colimit checks.

proof.text: By [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], the $I$-cell map $i$ is right anodyne. To include coproducts using exactly that definition, well-order the small indexing set of a coproduct of horns and attach its simplices one at a time; the colimit has the coproduct pushout universal property. This is a small transfinite composition of pushouts of right horns. Each pushout is degreewise injective by the set calculation in step 1; a continuous ordinal chain of injections has injective maps into its colimit, since equality of two old elements in the quotient is already witnessed at a common stage. Thus $i$ is degreewise injective. The lifting property of $r$ is exactly the right-fibration definition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Moreover $N$ is a quasicategory: project any inner horn to $M$, fill it there, and lift that simplex against $r$, since every inner horn is among its right horns. This uses the quasicategory definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.7 (014Z) and Variant 4.2.4.2; after simplicial opposite, these supply the right-horn closure, while this step records the closure and degreewise-injectivity checks for the explicit cellular factorization.

proof.text: For $a:K\to M$ write $\Gamma_a=\{h:K\times\Delta^n\to N\mid rh=a\operatorname{pr}_K\}$ in degree $n$, as in [lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-section-restriction]. Apply that node to the given equivalence $e:L\to M$ and to $r:N\to M$: restriction $e^*:\Gamma_{\mathrm{id}_M}\to\Gamma_e$ is a simplicial homotopy equivalence between Kan complexes. The factor $i$ is a vertex of $\Gamma_e$ because $ri=e$. Let $c$ be a homotopy inverse, and put $s=c(i)$. Then $s:M\to N$ satisfies $rs=\mathrm{id}_M$ exactly. Evaluating the homotopy $e^*c\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\Gamma_e}$ at $i$ gives an edge $P$ in $\Gamma_e$ with endpoints $se$ and $i$. Thus $P$ is a homotopy $L\times\Delta^1\to N$ whose projection to $M$ is constantly $e$.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.1.13 (02NC) and Definition 7.2.1.1, specialized to r and the vertex i; compare the displayed left-handed section argument in Corollary 7.2.1.14 (02ND), then take its right-handed dual.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to $r$ and the right anodyne inclusion $i$. Its trivial Kan fibration has source $\operatorname{Fun}(N,N)$ and target $\operatorname{Fun}(N,M)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(L,M)}\operatorname{Fun}(L,N)$. Give its target the edge $(r\operatorname{pr}_N,P)$, with the $\operatorname{Fun}(N,M)$ component constant at $r$. It lies in the displayed pullback because $rP=e\operatorname{pr}_L=ri\operatorname{pr}_L$. Prescribe the two boundary vertices in the source to be $sr$ and $\mathrm{id}_N$, in the endpoint order of $P$. Their restrictions to $L$ are $sri=se$ and $i$, and their composites with $r$ are both $r$ since $rs=\mathrm{id}_M$. The dimension-one boundary lift from [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] now gives $H:N\times\Delta^1\to N$ with endpoints $sr,\mathrm{id}_N$ and $rH=r\operatorname{pr}_N$ exactly.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4 (0154), whose statement includes the right-handed assertion, with the prescribed boundary of a 1-simplex; this expands the strict section homotopy in the displayed left-handed proof of Corollary 7.2.1.14 (02ND) after dualization.

proof.text: For every vertex $m\in M$, put $N_m=\{m\}\times_M N$. Apply the Kan-fiber clause of [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] with $E=F=N$, $B=M$, and both right fibrations equal to $r$; all three objects are quasicategories by hypothesis and step 2. Thus $N_m$ is Kan. The exact equations $rs=\mathrm{id}_M$ and $rH=r\operatorname{pr}_N$ ensure that $s(m)$ is a vertex of $N_m$ and that $H$ restricts to a homotopy on $N_m$ between its identity and the constant map at $s(m)$. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak] to $u:N_m\to\Delta^0$ and $v:\Delta^0\to N_m$ selecting $s(m)$: one inverse homotopy is this restriction of $H$, and the other is the constant homotopy on $\Delta^0$. It follows that $N_m$ is weakly contractible. This also verifies nonemptiness at every vertex of the base rather than assuming it.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.1.14 (02ND), whose displayed proof contracts each strict fiber in the left-handed case; apply the right-handed dual, and obtain weak contractibility via the existing realization homotopy-invariance node.

proof.text: The map $r$ is a right fibration by step 2, and all its strict vertex fibers are weakly contractible Kan complexes by step 5. Therefore [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers] makes $r$ a trivial Kan fibration in the full boundary-lifting sense, including dimension zero. Together with the exact equality $ri=e$, the right-anodyne degreewise injection $i$, and the small quasicategory $N$ already constructed, these are all the required conclusions.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.14 (01NU), (3) implies (1); its statement explicitly includes the right-handed case and completes the right-handed dual proof of Corollary 7.2.1.15 (02NE).

proof_origin.place: Expanded right-handed dual proof of Corollary 7.2.1.15 (02NE), whose displayed statement is left-handed, using the simplicial-opposite construction of Proposition 4.2.4.7 (014Z), the section-contraction proof of Corollary 7.2.1.14 (02ND), and Corollary 7.2.1.13 (02NC). Online sources read; no archived Kerodon source in literature/, so marked agent and archives WANTED in report.md.
